title: Fire Extinguishers
summary: Portable fire extinguishers must be approved, easy to reach, fully charged, and inspected. OSHA requires monthly visual checks and an annual maintenance check.
talking_points: Extinguishers must be mounted, located, and marked so you can reach them without getting hurt.
Only approved extinguishers can be used. Extinguishers must stay fully charged and in their designated place except during use.
Extinguishers are chosen by the class of fire expected (A, B, C, or D) and the size and degree of hazard.
Never use or provide extinguishers with carbon tetrachloride or chlorobromomethane agents.
Extinguishers must be visually inspected monthly.
Each extinguisher needs an annual maintenance check, and the date must be recorded.
Hydrostatic testing is done by trained persons at set intervals. Test again after corrosion, mechanical injury, damage, or burning in a fire.
When an extinguisher is out for maintenance or recharging, alternate equivalent protection must be provided.

Construction sites are covered by 29 CFR 1926.150(c). The monthly, annual, and hydrostatic test details above come from the general-industry standard (1910.157), so also follow the manufacturer schedule and your site fire protection plan.
site_hazards_to_check: Extinguishers blocked, moved from their place, or hard to reach
Gauge or pressure indicator showing not fully charged
Missing monthly inspection or annual maintenance date
Corrosion, dents, or other damage on the shell
Extinguisher type that does not match the fire class of nearby hazards
Extinguisher removed for service with no replacement
discussion_questions: Where is the nearest extinguisher, and is the path to it clear?
What class of fire could happen in our work area, and is this the right extinguisher?
When was this extinguisher last inspected, and who checks it?

attribution.notice: Adapted from OSHA published material. Reproduced with attribution for jobsite safety training; not an endorsement by OSHA.

flags: All points quote-accurate to 29 CFR 1910.157: charged/designated place, classes A-D, carbon tetrachloride ban, monthly visual, annual maintenance record, hydrostatic testing triggers, alternate protection.

FIX: 1910.157 is a general-industry standard with a partial construction equivalent (1926.150(c)); a point was added stating this so the talk does not present 1910 detail as the construction requirement. Both citations kept.
Non-blocking: 1926.150(c) extinguisher placement/rating rules are not spelled out here; consider adding them from the 1926 text. Attribution: osha.gov, public domain. No UK wording.
